## workbench

Applies to: Entire repository.

Decision map: [workbench](workbench/decision-map.md).

### Charter

Build a framework for organizing documents useful for agentic software development. Under this framework, collect best
practices into a shareable module which can be referenced from any project. Continuously innovate and refine to match
increasing agent intelligence and capabilities and project diversity and scope.

AI agents accelerate software creation causing human attention to increasingly bottleneck development. Delineate
documents which must be human-written and those requiring mandatory human review from the remainder of the project where
human review is optional at the discretion of the agent.

### Agent instructions

- [workbench:ADR-0](workbench/decisions/ADR-00.md): Humans write charters and approve ADR additions, changes, and
  removals before commit.

- [workbench:ADR-1](workbench/decisions/ADR-01.md): Read the listed decision maps after this file; open applicable ADRs
  before acting.

- [workbench:ADR-B](workbench/decisions/ADR-0B.md): Use authoritative tool and dependency pins; do not weaken checks
  merely to make changes pass.

- [workbench:ADR-D](workbench/decisions/ADR-0D.md): Run Workbench validation and applicable checks before completion;
  inspect `workbench checks`.

- [workbench:ADR-N](workbench/decisions/ADR-0N.md): Humans set `compatibility.required`; when false, migrate callers and
  data without shims.

- [workbench:ADR-R](workbench/decisions/ADR-0R.md): Change Guix/Nix environment versions or pins only on explicit human
  request.

- [workbench:ADR-U](workbench/decisions/ADR-0U.md): With benchd installed, use `benchctl hold` for builds, tests, and
  CPU-heavy work; ask before bypass.

- [workbench:ADR-V](workbench/decisions/ADR-0V.md): Preserve user data and active work; destructive resets require
  explicit authorization.
